jobs.title: Human Factors Engineer / Researcher
jobs.description:
Summary
  
  
At Apple, we create products that enrich people's lives — and our health products are central to that mission. Join one of the core teams helping to bring that vision to life. We are the Human Factors team, focusing on designing and conducting research to understand our users, informing the development and continuous improvement of impactful Apple health and wellness features. We are a dynamic, diverse, and collaborative team of researchers that work at the crossroads of research and product development. We are looking for an experienced human factors engineer / researcher to apply user-centered design principles to the research, design, and development of its health features. You will scope and execute the right research, uncover insights, and directly inform health product development. You'll have the unique opportunity to contribute to various products like Apple Watch, iPhone, AirPods, and the Health app and across broad health domains such as cardiac health, sleep, hearing health, women's health, and fitness.
  
  
Description
  
  
This role sits at the intersection of various disciplines in health product development, requiring close collaboration with designers, engineers, clinicians, and regulatory partners. The ideal candidate can rapidly build relationships and partner with cross-functional teams to understand and align on research priorities, while managing multiple concurrent projects. Success requires both rigorous scientific expertise in human factors research methodology and the ability to translate complex user experience problems and questions into well-designed research efforts. The ideal candidate can then ultimately convert that understanding into actionable insights that directly inform product design and development decisions.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree, with a concentration or extensive work in human factors, industrial engineering, cognitive psychology, biomechanics, experimental psychology, and/or human-computer interaction.
* 3 years of relevant research work experience managing human factors projects and driving research programs cross-functionally and independently.
* Expertise in creating rigorous experimental designs, utilizing scientific method, and prioritizing research insights that have implications for product design and development
* Expertise in conducting usability studies and interview techniques related to product use. Mixed methods expertise to combine quantitative and qualitative research approaches.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, attention to detail, patience, and aesthetic sensibility.
* Ability to distill research insights into presentations for engineers and designers in a concise way.
* Expertise with health software and hardware usability.

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* Master's/doctorate, with a concentration or extensive work in human factors, industrial engineering, cognitive psychology, biomechanics, experimental psychology, and/or human-computer interaction.
* 5 years of relevant work experience managing projects and driving research programs cross-functionally
* Relevant experience in medical device usability evaluations and documentation.
* Expertise in leading research programs informing wearables including smart watches, fitness trackers, and/or virtual reality headsets.
* Experience applying regulations and best practices for medical device human factors a plus (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices).
* Expertise in conducting and interpreting various statistical analyses (e.g., t-tests, ANOVA, regression, bootstrapping).

jobs.title: Lead User Experience Researcher - IT and Employee Productivity
jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. Today, we're tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. NVIDIA IT builds the products NVIDIANs use to get work done every day: the company intranet and mobile app, IT help and self-service, an AI personal assistant, and secure workspaces where employees run their own AI agents. We're hiring our first user experience researcher to answer a question that matters more every quarter: what makes people productive at NVIDIA, and what should we build, buy, or change so more people can work that way?

  

This is a senior, independent role with a long horizon. Our users are our colleagues, so access is never the bottleneck. You start with rich data: an annual IT survey with thousands of written comments from employees in 36 countries, support tickets, and product analytics. You'll set the research agenda, run the studies that matter most, and raise the research bar for the product managers and designers you work with.

  

**What you'll be doing:**

* Own a multi-quarter research program on how NVIDIANs work: what separates people who have adopted new ways of working, including AI tools, from those who haven't, and which tools, built or bought, would help the rest.
* Shape our core products. Find the fundamental changes that would make our intranet, IT help, and AI assistant more useful, starting from questions like "what does a typical work day at NVIDIA look like?"
* Pair field research (contextual inquiry, interviews, diary studies) with survey, support, and analytics data. Use AI to scale analysis without trading away validity.
* Bring rigor. Choose methods that hold up (reliability, validity, sampling), and help the team distinguish between decisions that benefit from research vs. decisions that can just be made.
* Raise the team's research craft. Coach PMs and designers on study design, interview guides, and live interviewing, and partner with designers on usability work
* Build the practice from zero: a participant panel, consent and confidentiality standards for research with colleagues (with HR and Legal), and an insights repository so research compounds instead of repeating.
Turn findings into decisions. Present clear recommendations to IT leadership, define experience and adoption metrics with PMs, and follow through until insights shape roadmaps, not just fixes.  

  

**What we need to see:**

* 12+ years in UX research or a closely related field, including leading strategic, multi-quarter research programs.
* Master's or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Anthropology, Sociology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Deep mixed-methods expertise: generative field research, survey design and analysis (including open text), and analysis of behavioral data.
* A portfolio or case studies showing research that changed strategy, roadmap, or investment decisions, not only feature details.
* Experience researching enterprise, internal, or workplace products used by employees.
* Proven ability to work as the first or only researcher on a team: set the agenda, say no to low-value studies, and coach others on research craft.
Clear writing and presentation that moves senior leaders to a decision.  

  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Research on AI tool adoption, knowledge-worker productivity, or how teams change the way they work.
* Internal IT, employee experience, or workplace technology research.
* Quantitative depth: SQL, R, or Python, and quasi-experimental designs (such as matched comparisons) that separate what drives adoption from what only correlates with it.
You've used LLMs to scale research synthesis and know where they fail.  

  

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technological world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative, and enjoy having fun, then what are you waiting for? Apply today!

jobs.description:
San Mateo, CA, United StatesDesign & CreativeID: 48944

  

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device.We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a User Researcher on the Platform & Foundation Design team, reporting directly to the Director of Design Strategy & Operations, you will generate actionable qualitative and quantitative insights that shape the platform and tools that empower our players, creators, and builders to bring their craft and vision to life. Embedded directly on product teams, you will conduct generative and evaluative research centered on how players engage, how creators build and grow, and how builders bring their ideas to life across the platform. You will tackle high-priority features, solve complex problems, and help translate foundational platform systems into intuitive, trustworthy, and scalable experiences. Partnering closely with Product, Product Design, Engineering, and Data Science, you will ensure user needs directly inform platform decisions while driving mutual value across players, creators, and builders.

**You will:**

* Execute end-to-end mixed-methods research projects to understand how players, creators, and builders use Foundation UI and tools, translating abstract user behaviors into clear product feature recommendations.
* Conduct foundational research to uncover key user pain points, mental models, and behaviors across creators, players, and builders to guide long-term UX strategy.
* Work with cross-functional stakeholders in Design, Product, Policy, Legal, Engineering, and Data Science to facilitate research discussions and give concise feedback to inform feature roadmaps and product vision.
* Partner with Analytics and Data Science to combine qualitative insights with behavioral platform data, building a holistic view of user engagement across the platform.
* Work in close collaboration with cross-functional teams to evolve research processes and foster a culture of inclusion, collaboration, and innovation.
* Have opportunities to present your research findings and strategic implications clearly to Product Group leadership.

**You have:**

* 5+ years of professional career experience as a UX or product researcher.
* A Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in HCI, psychology, marketing research, sociology, anthropology, or other social science field with an emphasis on research, or equivalent work experience.
* Knowledgeabout a variety of research methods. Is comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative methodology and can identify the correct methodology for the question at hand. Preferably has experience using software vendors like Qualtrics, database analysis with SQL and can conduct statistical analyses in SPSS, R or Python.
* Engaged in collaboration and sharing work frequently, inviting feedback from peers and manager or supervisor
* Solutions and a tuned thought process that ensure research will adequately answer questions and even challenge if the questions being asked are the right ones.
* The ability to articulate and research findings clearly through verbal, written, and visual communication.

jobs.title: Applied Researcher: On-Device Multimodal Reasoning
jobs.description:
Summary
  
  
The Video Computer Vision (VCV) organization is an applied research and engineering team developing real-time, on-device Computer Vision and Machine Perception technologies across Apple products. Within VCV, our team builds next-generation multimodal AI systems that combine on-device multimodal encoders, large language models, and foundation models to create intelligent systems capable of understanding, reasoning, and acting across language, vision, audio, and tools. Our work is deeply integrated into the Apple ecosystem, partnering across hardware, software, and ML teams to deliver real-time, scalable, and privacy-preserving experiences reaching millions of users.
  
  
Description
  
  
We are seeking an Applied Researcher with deep expertise in multimodal reasoning at small model scale — making vision-language models in the smaller regime (under ~10B parameters, down to sub-1B) think, plan, and act reliably under strict compute, memory, and latency constraints. In this role you will own the reasoning side of the on-device multimodal stack: designing compact VLMs that reason over images, video, and 3D scene content; compressing and distilling the reasoning process itself; and engineering the decoding and inference path that makes multi-step reasoning affordable on an Apple device. This role offers the unique opportunity to define what on-device intelligence looks like for hundreds of millions of users. You'll push the boundaries of what small models can achieve — enabling real-time multimodal understanding and multi-step reasoning without reliance on cloud connectivity. You'll collaborate with hardware teams, compiler engineers, and ML researchers to unlock capabilities that few organizations can deliver at Apple's scale and quality bar. This role spans multiple dimensions of efficient on-device reasoning — including VLM architecture and connector design, reasoning post-training (SFT/RL), chain-of-thought compression, speculative and structured decoding, visual token reduction, quantization and distillation, and hardware-aware inference optimization. A core focus of this role is efficient reasoning: compressed and latent chain-of-thought, reasoning distillation from frontier teachers, adaptive test-time compute (knowing when — and how long — to think), speculative and structured decoding, KV-cache compression, and visual-token efficiency. A second focus is reasoning over real-time visual perception experts. Rather than consuming pixels alone, the VLM should be able to invoke and reason over the outputs of specialist on-device vision models — feed-forward 3D scene and geometry estimators (VGGT-style reconstruction, depth, camera pose), human body and hand mesh/pose recovery, object detectors, localizers, and trackers — and fuse those structured, metric outputs into its reasoning about the scene. This raises real research questions: how to represent geometry, body parameters, and detections compactly in a token-budgeted context; how to schedule which experts run at which frame rate within a real-time budget; and how to train a small model to invoke, trust, and cross-check them. Efficiency is treated as a first-class metric here: reasoning quality is measured at a fixed latency, memory, and power budget.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, Computer Vision, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
* Strong foundation in deep learning, with specific experience in LLM or VLM training, post-training, or inference optimization
* Demonstrated experience working with multimodal models (vision-language models, multimodal LLMs) in resource-constrained environments, including hands-on work with reasoning quality, decoding, or model compression
* Proficiency in Python and modern deep learning frameworks (PyTorch preferred), with familiarity with inference and optimization toolchains (quantization, distillation, pruning — e.g., vLLM/SGLang, llama.cpp, MLX, CoreML)

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* PhD with research in efficient multimodal reasoning, LLM reasoning, model compression, efficient inference/decoding, or lightweight VLM architectures
* Experience training or post-training vision-language models end-to-end — connector/projector design, visual instruction tuning, resolution and token-budget trade-offs, small-model recipes
* Hands-on experience with reasoning techniques: chain-of-thought distillation and compression, latent/implicit reasoning, reward-guided decoding, RL for reasoning (GRPO, RLVR, STaR), or test-time compute allocation
* Expertise in decoding and serving optimizations: speculative decoding, structured/grammar-constrained generation, KV-cache quantization and eviction, continuous batching, long-context inference
* Experience combining LLMs with real-time perception models — 3D reconstruction and geometry (VGGT, DUSt3R/MASt3R-style, SLAM, monocular depth), human pose and body/hand mesh recovery (SMPL-family), detection, segmentation, or tracking — and with spatial or 3D-grounded reasoning and embodied/spatial VQA
* Experience deploying LLM or multimodal models on mobile or edge hardware (CoreML, MLX, TensorRT-LLM, or equivalent), with attention to ANE/GPU kernel and memory constraints
* Experience with quantization-aware training, mixed-precision inference, and knowledge distillation for vision-language models
* Familiarity with efficient vision encoders and self-supervised/joint-embedding pretraining (V-JEPA, I-JEPA, MAE, DINO/DINOv2, SigLIP, CLIP), Mamba/SSM vision backbones, or streaming architectures for real-time video with fixed memory budgets
* Interest in Video-LLMs, long-video reasoning, and world models for prediction and planning
* Publication record in top-tier venues is a plus (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ECCV, ACL, MLSys, ICRA, etc.)

### **Company Description**

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.

The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.

### **Job Description**

The Sr CRE uses their in-depth clinical, scientific, and technical knowledge to lead, collaborate with engineers, physicians, user experience researchers, and other internal and external stakeholders to develop new product concepts being incubated in early exploration. The individual brings their clinical device development expertise to new platform and technology development, and is responsible for identifying, documenting, and understanding user needs and subsequently communicating these needs to inform concept design and development. The Managing CRE is a technical individual that has aptitude and desire to expand into people management.

**Responsibilities**

**Advanced research lead and new product concept development**

* Identify key clinical needs for novel instrumentation, systems and devices
* Primary architect of clinical requirements, clinical risks and mitigations
* Participates on researching on disease states and medical technologies associated with new business opportunities for Intuitive and applying their in-depth knowledge to become an expert within the company on the new products being developed and their clinical application.
* Key stakeholder, collaborates closely with engineers and physicians to define clinical performance goals and potential risks for new products in early phase pf development.
* Manages, collects, and decipher VOC across various levels of management.
* Monitors and advices complex technical and clinical aspects of the product.
* Hire, develop and mentor a small group of CREs for the program.
* Collaborate with other organizations within the company as needed leading the clinical aspects of new programs and platform development: design engineering, regulatory, human factors, industrial design, training, marketing, and others.
* Develop and execute clinical de-risking pathways including both pre-clinical and clinical feasibility studies.

**Clinical innovation**

* Develop novel clinical models and metrics for technology evaluation and prototype performance assessment.
* Develop novel procedures and workflows for new technologies.

FAR.AI is a non-profit AI research institute working to ensure advanced AI is safe and beneficial for everyone. Our mission is to facilitate breakthrough AI safety research, advance global understanding of AI risks and solutions, and foster a coordinated global response.
  
  
Since our founding in July 2022, we've grown to 50+ staff, published 40+ academic papers, and convened leading AI safety events. Our work is recognized globally, with publications at premier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML including a Best Paper Honorable Mention in 2026, and ICLR, and features in the Financial Times, Nature News, Wired Magazine and MIT Technology Review. We conduct pre-deployment testing on behalf of frontier developers such as OpenAI, independent evaluations for governments including the EU AI Office, and publish the AI Security Leaderboard based on our red-teaming expertise. We help steer and grow the AI safety field through developing research roadmaps with renowned researchers such as Yoshua Bengio; running FAR.Labs, an AI safety-focused co-working space in Berkeley housing 40+ members; and supporting the community through targeted grants to technical researchers.

**About the team**
------------------

We explore promising research directions in AI safety and scale up only those showing a high potential for impact. When an approach proves effective, we develop it into a minimum viable demonstration and work with AI developers and governments to support real-world adoption.

Our recent and ongoing research includes:

* **Mitigating AI deception:** studying when lie detectors induce honesty or evasion, and developing approaches to state of the art falsehood detectors and sandbagging.

* **Applied Interpretability**: using interpretability to tackle concrete safety problems (better probes, backdoor detection, deception monitoring), aiming for fast feedback loops, often in collaboration with our other pods.

Summary
  
  
The Multimodal Intelligence Team is building the next generation of foundation models for Apple experiences. We are looking for a research scientist to advance the architectures, pre-training methods, and distillation techniques that make highly capable multimodal models practical across the Apple ecosystem. Our research spans the full foundation-model lifecycle: model architecture, pre-training objectives, data mixtures, optimization, scaling, distillation, and evaluation. A defining challenge of our work is to develop models that combine broad intelligence with the memory, latency, energy, and privacy requirements of on-device deployment. You will have the opportunity to shape new research directions, conduct ambitious experiments at scale, and translate successful ideas into foundation-model technologies that can reach Apple products. You will develop and evaluate new model architectures, pre-training objectives, data strategies, optimization methods, and teacher–student learning techniques. A major focus of the role will be the co-development of frontier models and efficient models for Apple silicon and on-device intelligence. jobs.title: AI Research Scientist: Multimodal Foundation Models - Architecture, Pre-Training & Distillation
jobs.description:
Summary
  
  
The Multimodal Intelligence Team is building the next generation of foundation models for Apple experiences. We are looking for a research scientist to advance the architectures, pre-training methods, and distillation techniques that make highly capable multimodal models practical across the Apple ecosystem. Our research spans the full foundation-model lifecycle: model architecture, pre-training objectives, data mixtures, optimization, scaling, distillation, and evaluation. A defining challenge of our work is to develop models that combine broad intelligence with the memory, latency, energy, and privacy requirements of on-device deployment. You will have the opportunity to shape new research directions, conduct ambitious experiments at scale, and translate successful ideas into foundation-model technologies that can reach Apple products. Where appropriate, this work may also lead to publications and the open sourcing of selected models, research artifacts, evaluations, or tools.
  
  
Description
  
  
In this role, you will investigate fundamental questions about how multimodal foundation models should be designed, trained, and distilled. You will develop and evaluate new model architectures, pre-training objectives, data strategies, optimization methods, and teacher–student learning techniques. Your work will explore how capabilities developed in large foundation models can be effectively transferred to smaller, more efficient models without treating distillation as an isolated downstream step. A major focus of the role will be the co-development of frontier models and efficient models for Apple silicon and on-device intelligence. This includes designing architectures that distill effectively, studying how teacher and student models should be trained together, and developing distillation methods that preserve reasoning, multimodal understanding, instruction following, and other important capabilities under constrained model capacity. Rather than treating deployment constraints as an afterthought, you will incorporate them into the research process—from early architecture experiments and pre-training through distillation and final model evaluation. You may thrive in this role if you: \* Want to invent new foundation-model architectures rather than only adapt existing models. \* Enjoy combining scientific ambition with real compute, memory, latency, and energy constraints. \* Believe that small and efficient models can be a frontier research problem, not merely a compression exercise. \* Are comfortable working across model research, data, systems, and hardware boundaries. \* Care about translating research into private, useful, and deeply integrated intelligent experiences. \* Want your work to have both product impact and a presence in the broader research community. Potential research directions include: \* Novel dense, recurrent, state-space, mixture-of-experts, and hybrid foundation-model architectures. \* Multimodal pre-training across language, images, video, audio, and sensor-derived representations. \* Compute-optimal model and data scaling, including data mixtures, curricula, tokenization, and training objectives. \* Architecture and algorithm co-design for memory-efficient and energy-efficient inference on Apple silicon. \* Offline and on-policy distillation using teacher-generated data, logits, representations, rationales, and other supervision signals.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* Hands-on experience designing, implementing, and running large-scale pre-training experiments for large language models.
* Experience with LLM pre-training topics such as model architecture, training objectives, data mixtures, tokenization, curricula, scaling, and optimization.
* Strong proficiency with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and distributed training systems.
* Experience evaluating pre-trained models across language understanding, reasoning, instruction following, or multimodal capabilities.
* Strong understanding of transformer-based architectures and current approaches to efficient or scalable foundation-model training.
* Master’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in machine learning, computer science, or a related technical field.

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* Experience contributing to major foundation-model pre-training efforts or leading architecture experiments that influenced a large training run.
* Research contributions in model architecture, scaling laws, multimodal pre-training, optimization, efficient attention, mixture-of-experts, state-space models, or related areas.
* Experience with knowledge distillation, including offline or off-policy distillation, on-policy distillation, self-distillation, sequence-level distillation, logic matching, or representation transfer.

* Experience with multimodal models spanning language, vision, video, audio, or other sensor modalities.

jobs.title: Senior Applied Research Scientist
jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

  

The Data and Agent Loop Lab is looking for a Senior Applied Research Scientist to help us build the next generation of multimodal search and curation systems for Physical AI. We're building the foundation for robots, autonomous vehicles, and intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and act in the real world. The data that trains these systems is as important as the models themselves, and the team sits at the center of that challenge. You'll work alongside world-class researchers and engineers to solve some of the hardest data problems in AI — at petabyte scale, across video, sensor, and language modalities. Your work will directly shape what our foundation models learn, and will help external customers build their own Physical AI pipelines on top of NVIDIA's platform.

  

**What you'll be doing:**

* Researching and designing multimodal search and curation systems optimized for Physical AI data — video, lidar, radar, text, and more. These systems help researchers and customers find, filter, and surface the highest-quality data — including embedding-based retrieval, quality scoring models, active learning loops, and relevance evaluation frameworks.
* Developing datasets, benchmarks, and experimental frameworks that establish guidelines for data curation in robotics and AV contexts — and publishing those findings so the community can benefit.
* Translating research into production-grade software; writing papers, blog posts, and documentation that help customers understand and apply our methods.
Staying current with the latest in data curation, information retrieval, and multimodal learning — and bringing those insights back to the team.  

  

**What we need to see:**

* M.S. or Ph.D. in a relevant field — machine learning, information retrieval, robotics, AV, or multimodal AI (or equivalent experience)
* 8+ years of industry or research experience.
* Deep understanding of the data challenges specific to Physical AI.
* Strong software engineering fundamentals — experience shipping production-grade systems, not just research prototypes.
* Clear, compelling communication: you can write a great paper and explain a tradeoff to a non-expert collaborator!
Experience mentoring junior researchers or engineers is a plus.  

  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Hands-on experience with data curation or search in robotics, autonomous vehicles, or embodied AI.
* Familiarity with model training pipelines and the role data quality plays in model performance.
* Experience with large-scale video data — collection, processing, and retrieval.
* Prior work on semantic or neural search (dense retrieval, CLIP-style embeddings, multimodal indexing).
Publications in top venues on data-centric AI, information retrieval, or multimodal learning.  

  

With competitive salaries and a generous benefits package ( www.nvidiabenefits.com ), we are widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us and, due to outstanding growth, our best-in-class engineering teams are rapidly growing. If you're a creative and autonomous engineer with a real passion for technology, we want to hear from you!

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits .

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 8, 2026.

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.

Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organizations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximizing these opportunities. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness the transformative power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist our scientists in both pRED and gRED to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide.

  

**The Opportunity**

At Genentech (gRED) and Roche (pRED), we’re applying software, robotics, and advanced AI to solve one of humanity’s hardest challenges: building fully autonomous, self-healing laboratories for lights-out drug discovery. Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. The Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) and the Data and Digital Catalyst (DDC) team are building the foundational platform for autonomous labs—turning frontier AI models, rich physical telemetry, and multi-vendor robotics into resilient, intelligent systems that run complex science unattended around the clock to deliver life-saving medicines to patients faster than ever before.

As a Senior Multimodal Machine Learning Scientist, you will be the hands-on technical lead and architect developing intelligent systems for autonomous laboratories. Your work will span computer vision and multimodal perception, predictive modeling, agentic systems, and closed-loop experimentation, for example, unifying camera feeds with rich physical telemetry to give lab systems situational awareness and autonomous recovery capabilities. You will build and deploy models and end-to-end ML pipelines, from data collection and model development to evaluation and deployment, helping pioneer the next generation of intelligent laboratory infrastructure at global scale.

**In this role, you will:**

  

* Develop and fine-tune state-of-the-art vision models (VLMs, DinoV2, SAM, custom detection/segmentation) to perform real-time visual quality control across lab workcells (e.g., liquid level sensing, tip verification, labware orientation, spill/foam detection).
* Develop multimodal models that integrate camera feeds and video streams with time-series sensor telemetry, system logs, assay metadata, and other laboratory data to catch and understand physical failure modes.
* Build predictive AI models on rich analytical data (spectroscopy, plate-readers, chromatography) to quantify assay quality and support closed-loop experimental decision-making.
* Build the data and ML pipelines needed to support these systems end-to-end, including image/video and sensor data collection, curation, processing, labeling, model training, deployment, monitoring, and iterative improvement.
* Build agentic pipelines that interpret lab data, reason through multi-step experimental workflows, and execute autonomous recovery decisions.
* Build rigorous evaluation suites (evals) to systematically benchmark model and agent accuracy, robustness, and decision safety in drug discovery labs.
* Deploy and optimize scalable ML inference and monitoring infrastructure that is low-latency and can support diverse models, instruments, and scientific use cases.

**Who you are:**

  

* MS/PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, AI, or a related quantitative field with 3+ years of hands-on experience deploying production ML systems or translational research models.
* Passion for translating frontier AI into biological workflows and real-world therapeutic breakthroughs.
* Strong background in Computer Vision and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), with hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or evaluating visual perception architectures (e.g., PyTorch, OpenCV, torchvision, object detection/segmentation, vision-text transformers).
* Strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and data analysis, with hands-on experience developing and deploying predictive and data-driven models.
* Proven track record building and deploying multimodal models that combine camera feeds/image streams with unstructured physical data (sensor logs, time-series, tabular scientific data).
* Hands-on experience building, orchestrating, or tuning agent harnesses.
* Demonstrated mastery in building comprehensive evaluation pipelines (evals) to benchmark model and agent accuracy, robustness, and safety in production environments.
* Demonstrated ability to work across disciplines and translate scientific requirements into practical ML systems, collaborating with scientists, automation/robotics engineers, and software engineers.

**Preferred, but not required**

  

* Experience with synthetic vision data generation, video-based anomaly detection, or edge-vision deployment.
* Familiarity with lab automation hardware, analytical instruments (liquid handlers, plate readers, HPLC), or industrial IoT telemetry.
* Exposure to Bayesian optimization, active learning, reinforcement learning, or Design of Experiments (DoE) for closed-loop experimentation.
* Public GitHub/GitLab portfolio showcasing production ML pipelines, computer vision projects, agentic frameworks/evals, or multimodal models.

Summary
  
  
At Apple, we don’t just build products — we build experiences fueled by world-class data. The Human-centered AI team within Apple Services Engineering is looking for an ML Evaluation Specialist, Human Data to join our Data Quality and Operations division to spearhead complex, multi-stakeholder operations that specialize in data collection, curation, annotation, and human evaluation efforts across Apple Music, App Store, TV+, Podcasts, and Books.

In this role, you will own the operational strategy and continuous improvement of large-scale, multilingual human data programs, from designing onboarding scaffolds that progressively build annotator calibration, to analyzing annotator behavior patterns to identify where automation can offload low-judgment decisions, to enforcing quality frameworks that close the loop between annotator struggle and task redesign. You will identify where human judgment is essential and where it could be better directed, then build the scaffolding, automation, and feedback systems that let annotators focus their cognitive energy where it matters most. Because this work cuts across engineering, data science, research, procurement, and legal, a critical part of the role is serving as the connective tissue between teams who each own a piece of this space, aligning on shared standards, surfacing gaps, and ensuring that insights from the annotation layer inform upstream decisions about task design and tooling. You are comfortable designing and deploying sophisticated data pipelines in the morning, and then seamlessly transitioning to present comprehensive quality rectification strategies to stakeholders in the afternoon. new_jobs.title: Lead User Experience Researcher - IT and Employee Productivity
new_jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. Today, we're tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. NVIDIA IT builds the products NVIDIANs use to get work done every day: the company intranet and mobile app, IT help and self-service, an AI personal assistant, and secure workspaces where employees run their own AI agents. We're hiring our first user experience researcher to answer a question that matters more every quarter: what makes people productive at NVIDIA, and what should we build, buy, or change so more people can work that way?

  

This is a senior, independent role with a long horizon. Our users are our colleagues, so access is never the bottleneck. You start with rich data: an annual IT survey with thousands of written comments from employees in 36 countries, support tickets, and product analytics. You'll set the research agenda, run the studies that matter most, and raise the research bar for the product managers and designers you work with.

  

**What you'll be doing:**

* Own a multi-quarter research program on how NVIDIANs work: what separates people who have adopted new ways of working, including AI tools, from those who haven't, and which tools, built or bought, would help the rest.
* Shape our core products. Find the fundamental changes that would make our intranet, IT help, and AI assistant more useful, starting from questions like "what does a typical work day at NVIDIA look like?"
* Pair field research (contextual inquiry, interviews, diary studies) with survey, support, and analytics data. Use AI to scale analysis without trading away validity.
* Bring rigor. Choose methods that hold up (reliability, validity, sampling), and help the team distinguish between decisions that benefit from research vs. decisions that can just be made.
* Raise the team's research craft. Coach PMs and designers on study design, interview guides, and live interviewing, and partner with designers on usability work
* Build the practice from zero: a participant panel, consent and confidentiality standards for research with colleagues (with HR and Legal), and an insights repository so research compounds instead of repeating.
Turn findings into decisions. Present clear recommendations to IT leadership, define experience and adoption metrics with PMs, and follow through until insights shape roadmaps, not just fixes.  

  

**What we need to see:**

* 12+ years in UX research or a closely related field, including leading strategic, multi-quarter research programs.
* Master's or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Anthropology, Sociology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Deep mixed-methods expertise: generative field research, survey design and analysis (including open text), and analysis of behavioral data.
* A portfolio or case studies showing research that changed strategy, roadmap, or investment decisions, not only feature details.
* Experience researching enterprise, internal, or workplace products used by employees.
* Proven ability to work as the first or only researcher on a team: set the agenda, say no to low-value studies, and coach others on research craft.
Clear writing and presentation that moves senior leaders to a decision.  

  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Research on AI tool adoption, knowledge-worker productivity, or how teams change the way they work.
* Internal IT, employee experience, or workplace technology research.
* Quantitative depth: SQL, R, or Python, and quasi-experimental designs (such as matched comparisons) that separate what drives adoption from what only correlates with it.
You've used LLMs to scale research synthesis and know where they fail.  

  

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technological world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative, and enjoy having fun, then what are you waiting for? Apply today!

new_jobs.title: Applied Researcher: On-Device Multimodal Reasoning
new_jobs.description:
Summary
  
  
The Video Computer Vision (VCV) organization is an applied research and engineering team developing real-time, on-device Computer Vision and Machine Perception technologies across Apple products. Within VCV, our team builds next-generation multimodal AI systems that combine on-device multimodal encoders, large language models, and foundation models to create intelligent systems capable of understanding, reasoning, and acting across language, vision, audio, and tools. Our work is deeply integrated into the Apple ecosystem, partnering across hardware, software, and ML teams to deliver real-time, scalable, and privacy-preserving experiences reaching millions of users.
  
  
Description
  
  
We are seeking an Applied Researcher with deep expertise in multimodal reasoning at small model scale — making vision-language models in the smaller regime (under ~10B parameters, down to sub-1B) think, plan, and act reliably under strict compute, memory, and latency constraints. In this role you will own the reasoning side of the on-device multimodal stack: designing compact VLMs that reason over images, video, and 3D scene content; compressing and distilling the reasoning process itself; and engineering the decoding and inference path that makes multi-step reasoning affordable on an Apple device. This role offers the unique opportunity to define what on-device intelligence looks like for hundreds of millions of users. You'll push the boundaries of what small models can achieve — enabling real-time multimodal understanding and multi-step reasoning without reliance on cloud connectivity. You'll collaborate with hardware teams, compiler engineers, and ML researchers to unlock capabilities that few organizations can deliver at Apple's scale and quality bar. This role spans multiple dimensions of efficient on-device reasoning — including VLM architecture and connector design, reasoning post-training (SFT/RL), chain-of-thought compression, speculative and structured decoding, visual token reduction, quantization and distillation, and hardware-aware inference optimization. A core focus of this role is efficient reasoning: compressed and latent chain-of-thought, reasoning distillation from frontier teachers, adaptive test-time compute (knowing when — and how long — to think), speculative and structured decoding, KV-cache compression, and visual-token efficiency. A second focus is reasoning over real-time visual perception experts. Rather than consuming pixels alone, the VLM should be able to invoke and reason over the outputs of specialist on-device vision models — feed-forward 3D scene and geometry estimators (VGGT-style reconstruction, depth, camera pose), human body and hand mesh/pose recovery, object detectors, localizers, and trackers — and fuse those structured, metric outputs into its reasoning about the scene. This raises real research questions: how to represent geometry, body parameters, and detections compactly in a token-budgeted context; how to schedule which experts run at which frame rate within a real-time budget; and how to train a small model to invoke, trust, and cross-check them. Efficiency is treated as a first-class metric here: reasoning quality is measured at a fixed latency, memory, and power budget.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, Computer Vision, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
* Strong foundation in deep learning, with specific experience in LLM or VLM training, post-training, or inference optimization
* Demonstrated experience working with multimodal models (vision-language models, multimodal LLMs) in resource-constrained environments, including hands-on work with reasoning quality, decoding, or model compression
* Proficiency in Python and modern deep learning frameworks (PyTorch preferred), with familiarity with inference and optimization toolchains (quantization, distillation, pruning — e.g., vLLM/SGLang, llama.cpp, MLX, CoreML)

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* PhD with research in efficient multimodal reasoning, LLM reasoning, model compression, efficient inference/decoding, or lightweight VLM architectures
* Experience training or post-training vision-language models end-to-end — connector/projector design, visual instruction tuning, resolution and token-budget trade-offs, small-model recipes
* Hands-on experience with reasoning techniques: chain-of-thought distillation and compression, latent/implicit reasoning, reward-guided decoding, RL for reasoning (GRPO, RLVR, STaR), or test-time compute allocation
* Expertise in decoding and serving optimizations: speculative decoding, structured/grammar-constrained generation, KV-cache quantization and eviction, continuous batching, long-context inference
* Experience combining LLMs with real-time perception models — 3D reconstruction and geometry (VGGT, DUSt3R/MASt3R-style, SLAM, monocular depth), human pose and body/hand mesh recovery (SMPL-family), detection, segmentation, or tracking — and with spatial or 3D-grounded reasoning and embodied/spatial VQA
* Experience deploying LLM or multimodal models on mobile or edge hardware (CoreML, MLX, TensorRT-LLM, or equivalent), with attention to ANE/GPU kernel and memory constraints
* Experience with quantization-aware training, mixed-precision inference, and knowledge distillation for vision-language models
* Familiarity with efficient vision encoders and self-supervised/joint-embedding pretraining (V-JEPA, I-JEPA, MAE, DINO/DINOv2, SigLIP, CLIP), Mamba/SSM vision backbones, or streaming architectures for real-time video with fixed memory budgets
* Interest in Video-LLMs, long-video reasoning, and world models for prediction and planning
* Publication record in top-tier venues is a plus (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ECCV, ACL, MLSys, ICRA, etc.)

new_jobs.title: People Research Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission *to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence*. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

**About the Role:**

We're looking for a People Research Scientist to join our People Science and Workforce Intelligence team. You'll be the research lead for the wider People organization bringing scientific rigor to the questions that matter most as Crusoe scales: how well do we hire, what makes people stay, grow and do great work here, and which of our investments actually make a difference.

The role sits where organizational science, behavioral research and people strategy meet. You'll build frameworks and run systematic research that shape people decisions at one of the fastest-growing companies in AI infrastructure.

**You'll study a workforce few people science teams ever see. Our workforce spans a high-growth tech company, a distributed manufacturing operation, and a field organization building and running data centers internationally.**

**What You'll Be Working On:**

* **Own research design and scientific inquiry**

  + Form and test hypotheses about people programs, employee behavior and workforce outcomes using rigorous experimental and quasi-experimental methods.
  + Run longitudinal studies to learn what creates long-term success, engagement, and retention as we scale.
  + Synthesize external research and industry evidence on people interventions to find best practices and gaps.
  + Partner cross-functionally to design and run systematic studies on employee experience, manager effectiveness and organizational health across corporate, engineering and field teams.
  + Apply sound research ethics and data privacy practices to all employee research.
* **Program effectiveness and impact**

  + Build evaluation plans into people programs from the start, including onboarding, manager development, learning, recognition, and retention or compensation programs.
  + Estimate program impact using quasi-experimental methods such as staged rollouts, difference-in-differences, matching and regression discontinuity.
  + Define success measures and leading indicators that tie people programs to business outcomes such as time to productivity, retention of critical talent, and site readiness.
  + Give clear recommendations on what to scale, change or stop.
* **Selection science and hiring research**

The GenMedia Safety team develops the data and algorithmic solutions that define the safety and behavior of GDM’s latest image and video generation models. In this role, you will build and deploy innovations that impact millions of users. This is a collaborative role focused on delivering effective outcomes across our internal and external platforms.

Artificial Intelligence could be one of humanity’s most useful inventions. At DeepMind, we are a team of scientists, engineers, machine learning experts and more, working together to advance the state of the art in artificial intelligence. You will be comfortable both with designing approaches to new research questions and executing the technical implementation of research ideas. You will have the opportunity to work directly on Nano Banana (GDM's core image generation capability), OMNI (GDM's core video generation capability), and successor GenMedia models. new_jobs.title: AI Research Scientist: Multimodal Foundation Models - Architecture, Pre-Training & Distillation
new_jobs.description:
Summary
  
  
The Multimodal Intelligence Team is building the next generation of foundation models for Apple experiences. We are looking for a research scientist to advance the architectures, pre-training methods, and distillation techniques that make highly capable multimodal models practical across the Apple ecosystem. Our research spans the full foundation-model lifecycle: model architecture, pre-training objectives, data mixtures, optimization, scaling, distillation, and evaluation. A defining challenge of our work is to develop models that combine broad intelligence with the memory, latency, energy, and privacy requirements of on-device deployment. You will have the opportunity to shape new research directions, conduct ambitious experiments at scale, and translate successful ideas into foundation-model technologies that can reach Apple products. Where appropriate, this work may also lead to publications and the open sourcing of selected models, research artifacts, evaluations, or tools.
  
  
Description
  
  
In this role, you will investigate fundamental questions about how multimodal foundation models should be designed, trained, and distilled. You will develop and evaluate new model architectures, pre-training objectives, data strategies, optimization methods, and teacher–student learning techniques. Your work will explore how capabilities developed in large foundation models can be effectively transferred to smaller, more efficient models without treating distillation as an isolated downstream step. A major focus of the role will be the co-development of frontier models and efficient models for Apple silicon and on-device intelligence. This includes designing architectures that distill effectively, studying how teacher and student models should be trained together, and developing distillation methods that preserve reasoning, multimodal understanding, instruction following, and other important capabilities under constrained model capacity. Rather than treating deployment constraints as an afterthought, you will incorporate them into the research process—from early architecture experiments and pre-training through distillation and final model evaluation. You may thrive in this role if you: \* Want to invent new foundation-model architectures rather than only adapt existing models. \* Enjoy combining scientific ambition with real compute, memory, latency, and energy constraints. \* Believe that small and efficient models can be a frontier research problem, not merely a compression exercise. \* Are comfortable working across model research, data, systems, and hardware boundaries. \* Care about translating research into private, useful, and deeply integrated intelligent experiences. \* Want your work to have both product impact and a presence in the broader research community. Potential research directions include: \* Novel dense, recurrent, state-space, mixture-of-experts, and hybrid foundation-model architectures. \* Multimodal pre-training across language, images, video, audio, and sensor-derived representations. \* Compute-optimal model and data scaling, including data mixtures, curricula, tokenization, and training objectives. \* Architecture and algorithm co-design for memory-efficient and energy-efficient inference on Apple silicon. \* Offline and on-policy distillation using teacher-generated data, logits, representations, rationales, and other supervision signals.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* Hands-on experience designing, implementing, and running large-scale pre-training experiments for large language models.
* Experience with LLM pre-training topics such as model architecture, training objectives, data mixtures, tokenization, curricula, scaling, and optimization.
* Strong proficiency with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and distributed training systems.

* Master’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in machine learning, computer science, or a related technical field, and a minimum of 6 years relevant experience.

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* Experience contributing to major foundation-model pre-training efforts or leading architecture experiments that influenced a large training run.
* Research contributions in model architecture, scaling laws, multimodal pre-training, optimization, efficient attention, mixture-of-experts, state-space models, or related areas.

new_jobs.title: Research Engineer, ML for EDA
new_jobs.description:
**Position Overview**
---------------------

We are hiring Research Engineers to apply machine learning to electronic design automation (EDA). Power, performance, and area are the central tradeoffs in chip design, and getting them right takes deep expertise and long iterations through EDA tools. You'll own research projects that apply ML to these problems across the design flow, from problem definition through data, modeling, and evaluation, and turn successful results into capabilities in the ChipAgents platform. You'll work alongside other ML researchers, software engineers, and hardware experts.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Lead research projects that apply machine learning to power, performance, and area problems in chip design, from problem definition to production.
* Build datasets and benchmarks from EDA tool flows across a range of designs and technologies.
* Design, train, and evaluate ML models on hardware design data.
* Form clear hypotheses, set strong baselines, and distinguish meaningful improvements from benchmark noise.
* Work with engineering and product teams to bring research results into the ChipAgents platform.
* Write well-architected, maintainable code that others can build on.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* MS or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience in industry.
* Strong ML fundamentals and hands-on experience designing, training, and debugging deep learning models in PyTorch or similar platforms.
* Working knowledge of the digital design flow, from RTL through synthesis, place and route, and timing and power analysis.
* Experience running and scripting EDA tools, commercial or open source.
* Strong Python software engineering skills and a record of writing research code that others build on.
* Ability to identify the crux of an ambiguous research problem, choose the experiments that matter, and explain results clearly to ML and hardware engineers.
* Self-directed and ambitious, with strong ownership and good judgment about when work is ready to ship.

**Nice to Haves**
-----------------

* Publications at EDA venues such as DAC, ICCAD, MLCAD, or ISPD, or at ML venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, or ICLR.
* Prior work applying ML to EDA or chip design problems.
* Experience with ML on graphs or other structured data.
* Industry experience in physical design, timing closure, or power analysis.
* Experience with LLMs or agent systems.
* Experience running large-scale training or data generation on compute clusters.

**Why ChipAgents**
------------------

* Your research ships to semiconductor companies and gets tested on their designs as well as public benchmarks.
* Own research problems end to end, with software engineers who take your work into production and customer environments so you can stay focused on research.
* Work alongside ML researchers and chip design veterans, and help set the research direction of a fast-growing team.
* Publish and present your work at conferences where appropriate.

**Equal Opportunity**
---------------------

ChipAgents is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* **$150K/yr – $350K/yr** base salary + equity. We are open to discuss above-scale compensation with exceptional candidates on a case-by-case basis.
* Unlimited PTO and full benefits (medical, vision, dental, 401k).
* Two engineering-centric offices with free parking, private gym, and free lunch, drinks and snacks.

We're building the foundation for robots, autonomous vehicles, and intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and act in the real world. The data that trains these systems is as important as the models themselves, and the team sits at the center of that challenge. You'll work alongside world-class researchers and engineers to solve some of the hardest data problems in AI — at petabyte scale, across video, sensor, and language modalities.
